title: Sunset Session

conditions.headline: Alphabet Wipeout Chops Up Tech, Small Caps Ride It In
conditions.summary: Alphabet's worst day since its 2004 debut dragged the Nasdaq down about 1.4 percent, while the S&P 500 and Dow slipped only modestly. Small caps, health care and financials caught a bid as money rotated out of software.

sections.title: Closing Bell
items: The S&P 500 fell 0.3% to about 7,720, ending a three-day winning streak.
The Nasdaq Composite dropped 1.4% to about 26,185, hit hardest by Alphabet and software stocks.
The Dow slipped 0.25% to about 52,343 after opening down nearly 400 points, while the Russell 2000 rose 1.0% to about 2,859.
Stocks spent most of the day in the red, then recovered part of their losses in the final hour.
Software was the weakest corner, with the IGV software fund down about 4%; health care hit a record high and financials and real estate also drew buyers.

sections.title: Macro & Fed
items: Third-quarter GDP grew at a 3.4% annual pace, up from 2.2% in the second quarter and above forecasts.
PCE inflation rose to 3.6% from a year earlier, up from 3.4%; core PCE rose 0.3% for the month, as expected.
Weekly jobless claims fell to 194,000, below the 198,000 expected.
The Fed held rates at 3.75% to 4.00% on Wednesday in a 10-2 vote, with two officials wanting a hike; markets price roughly an 80% chance of a December hike.
The 10-year Treasury yield ended near 4.99%, down about 5 basis points; gold slipped to about $4,038 and bitcoin fell below $80,000.

sections.title: Biggest Movers
items: GOOGL (Alphabet): -12.6% — sales fell short and heavy AI spending outran cash flow, erasing roughly $500 billion in market value.
NOW (ServiceNow): -26.5% — its results sparked a broad selloff in software stocks.
FTNT (Fortinet): -20.1% — it cut its service revenue forecast even as it raised its overall 2026 revenue outlook.
MRVL (Marvell): -13.2% — reports said it is in advanced talks to buy Lumentum.
LLY (Eli Lilly): +6.4% — third-quarter revenue jumped 39% to $24.4 billion and it raised its full-year forecast.
ADT (ADT): +33.4% — agreed to be bought by Thrive Holdings for $10 a share in cash.
CROX (Crocs): +25.5% — raised its 2026 outlook.
XRX (Xerox): -40.3% — cut its full-year forecasts.

sections.title: Earnings Today & Tonight
items: Caterpillar beat third-quarter estimates but fell as much as 12% intraday on a disappointing fourth-quarter outlook.
Amazon fell about 7% after hours: AWS sales grew 39%, but heavy AI spending pushed trailing free cash flow below zero.
Intel sank about 18% after hours as its fourth-quarter revenue guide of $15 billion to $16 billion came in below the roughly $17 billion expected.
Rivian jumped after hours on revenue of $2.16 billion, above estimates, and a raised full-year outlook.
Sandisk rose about 2% after hours on $11 billion in quarterly revenue and an eight-for-one stock split.

sections.title: Business News
items: DoorDash agreed to buy Instacart for $65 a share, mostly in cash, a deal valued around $17 billion; DoorDash shares rose about 5.6%.
Thrive Holdings agreed to buy home-security company ADT for $10 a share in cash.
Alphabet's drop ranks as the second-largest one-day loss of market value for a US-listed company, behind Nvidia's in January 2025.
The European Central Bank held its deposit rate at 2.50%, as expected.
The average 30-year fixed mortgage rate eased to 7.24%.

sections.title: On Deck
items: 7:30 AM CT: Employment Cost Index for the third quarter.
Before the open: ExxonMobil and Chevron report third-quarter results.
Before the open: AbbVie reports, with its call at 8:00 AM CT.
Markets digest the after-hours moves in Amazon and Intel.

script: Cowabunga! This is Surf Daddy, your local Kahuna, live from Surfside USA to all you Trade Wind surfers from the Gulf Coast to the North Shore. It's Thursday, October twenty-ninth, twenty twenty-six, and this is your Sunset Session, the full wrap of today's market. The sun is sinking low over the water, the sky is going orange, and we are paddling out for the last set of the day. Gus the wonder dog spent the afternoon chasing sandpipers down the beach, and now he's back in the cabana, all sandy and proud. Say good evening to the crew, Gus! Alright, let's ride. Today's conditions were choppy, so I'm calling it a fair session. The S and P five hundred slipped three tenths of a percent to about seven thousand seven hundred twenty, ending a three day winning streak. The Nasdaq took a gnarly hit, down about one point four percent to roughly twenty-six thousand one hundred eighty-five. The Dow eased a quarter percent to about fifty-two thousand three hundred forty-three, after opening down nearly four hundred points. But the small caps found their own little break, with the Russell two thousand up one percent. The big wipeout was Alphabet. The stock fell about twelve and a half percent, its worst day since it went public in two thousand four. Sales came up short, and all that A I spending outran its cash. That knocked out roughly five hundred billion dollars in market value. Software got pulled under too. ServiceNow sank about twenty-six percent, and Fortinet dropped about twenty percent. Money paddled over to health care, which hit a record high, plus financials and real estate. Eli Lilly caught a beautiful wave, up more than six percent after revenue jumped thirty-nine percent and it raised its forecast. Gus, that one earns a biscuit! Here you go, buddy! Now the wind and weather. The economy grew at a three point four percent pace last quarter, stronger than expected. But PCE inflation climbed to three point six percent from a year ago. Jobless claims dropped to one hundred ninety-four thousand. After yesterday's Fed hold, traders still see good odds of a rate hike in December. The ten year Treasury yield finished near four point nine nine percent, down about five basis points. Oil sat near one hundred three dollars, gold slipped to about four thousand thirty-eight, and bitcoin fell under eighty thousand. The fear gauge, the VIX, ticked up to about seventeen. In the lineup, A D T jumped thirty-three percent on a buyout from Thrive Holdings. Crocs rose about twenty-five percent on a better outlook. Xerox wiped out, down forty percent after cutting its forecast. On the tide chart tonight, Amazon fell about seven percent after hours. Cloud sales grew thirty-nine percent, but heavy A I spending drained its cash flow. Intel sank about eighteen percent on a soft revenue guide. Rivian jumped after a revenue beat and a raised outlook. In beach talk, DoorDash agreed to buy Instacart for sixty-five dollars a share, about seventeen billion dollars. Tomorrow's forecast: the Employment Cost Index lands at seven thirty A M Central, and ExxonMobil, Chevron and AbbVie report before the open. Catch the Dawn Patrol in the morning for the opening swell. Remember, the soul surfers who stay patient through choppy days are the ones still standing on their boards. Got a stock, an E T F or a futures contract on your mind? Type it in the Check a Wave box on the page, and Surf Daddy will call it for you. Wax that board for tomorrow. This is information, not advice. This is Surf Daddy and Gus the wonder dog saying, if in doubt, paddle out!
